claims.text: The trip deviated on the platform's own measurement. The GPS trace records trace_distance_km of 16.2 km against a booked optimal_distance_km of 12.0 km — an excess of 4.2 km, or 35% — which clears both POL-RD-01 tests: greater than 20% of the optimal distance and greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms. The deviation is therefore ESTABLISHED on this trip's own evidence, and the driver's assertion that he 'followed the road available' does not meet either test in reverse.

The trace is clean for policy purposes, so no impairment consequences attach. It carries 205 fixes at a 10-second interval with 100% coverage, an empty gaps list and max_gap_sec of 0. None of POL-RD-07 limbs (a) to (c) fires, the deviation may be established on the gps_trace alone, and no independent corroboration is needed to carry it.

The rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08 is discharged. The trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry trip_id TRP-09111 and describe the same journey, and the excess measured above meets the POL-RD-01 threshold from an unimpaired trace. The burden therefore shifts to the driver to point to a specific artifact and clause.

No rider instruction exonerates the driver under POL-RD-04. The chat log holds exactly two messages: the rider at 08:12:00 writing 'The navigation route was left after Pioneer Road. Please return to the booked route', and the driver at 08:12:35 replying 'I am following the road ahead'. There is no waypoint_hint and no road or place requested by the rider, so POL-RD-04 is unavailable and the whole excess stands.

No traffic advisory excuses the deviation under POL-RD-03. The only advisory artifact, EV-ADVIS-09111-01, is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT — it carries no payload, so no road closure or contraflow is on file for the booked route and window, and POL-RD-03(a) to (c) cannot be satisfied. The artifact is cited for its absence, which is itself a citable fact.

Neither endpoint was amended, so POL-RD-05 gives the driver no relief and the baseline remains the booked 12.0 km. pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are null and amended_optimal_distance_km is null, so no re-quote exists and no distance falls to be excluded on this ground.

This was not a pooled trip, so POL-RD-12's matched-itinerary baseline does not apply. vehicle_type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, and solo_optimal_distance_km is null; the booked optimal of 12.0 km is the correct baseline for the threshold test and for the recomputation.

The refund is arithmetic, not discretionary. The fare model is METERED and quoted_fare_sgd is null, so POL-RD-02 governs and POL-RD-11 does not: charged_total is SGD 33.36; recomputed_fare is SGD 24.2240 (base 3.80 + 0.75 x 12.0 km + 0.28 x 24.0 min = 19.520, surged at 1.2 to 23.424, + 0.80 platform fee + 1.00 on-optimal-route ERP - 1.00 promo discount); the refund is 33.36 - 24.2240 = SGD 9.1360, rounded UP to SGD 9.15. That is 27.4% of charged_total, below the 90% full-refund share, so the outcome is a PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 9.15 — precisely the amount the rider contests.

The off-route gantry charge is already captured and must not be added twice. The SGD 2.00 'Tuas South Avenue 8 loop' line is flagged on_optimal_route false and sits outside the recomputed fare, which includes only the SGD 1.00 'Pioneer Road inbound' gantry lying on the optimal route. Under POL-RD-09(1) that off-route ERP is comprehended in the POL-RD-02 refund and is itemised for transparency only — it is never added on top of the POL-RD-02 figure.

The record confirms the stakes for the rider, who filed this dispute. payment_status is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.0, so the rider is presently carrying the full SGD 33.36. NO_ACTION would leave that charge standing and the rider out of pocket for a deviation the platform's own trace measures at 35%; only a refund leaves the rider not carrying the disputed excess.

No enhanced corroboration is demanded of this rider. rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0, far below the four-claim trigger in POL-RD-08, and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0; the rider is not a serial unsubstantiated claimant, and no additional source beyond the trace is required to carry this claim.

The driver's statement does not discharge the shifted burden. 'I followed the road available to me. The rider did not request any stop' names no traffic_advisory, cites no artifact and invokes no clause; under POL-RD-08 a general assertion unsupported by an advisory ID carries no weight, and the rider's own on-trip message records that the driver was told he had left the booked route and continued anyway.

claims.text: The driver does not dispute that his own trace establishes an excess: 16.2 km driven against the 12.0 km booked optimal route is 4.2 km and 35%, and both POL-RD-01 establishment tests are met. But the same figures keep this trip out of the MATERIAL band, because 35% is below the 50% figure and 4.2 km is below the 8.0 km figure. The rider's description of the trip as 'substantially longer' therefore overstates it: the deviation is established but not material, the POL-RD-06 driver-profile check is not engaged, and the POL-RD-06(b) uplift to FULL_REFUND is unavailable.

Even if the profile check were run, the only two counters POL-RD-06 permits clear the driver: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 across driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 610 - no flags against the 3-flag threshold, and a zero ratio against the 0.05 threshold. There is no repeat-deviation pattern, so POL-RD-06(a) tie-breaking, POL-RD-06(b) uplift and POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral all fail at the first step. I rely on those two fields alone, as POL-GEN-01 requires; the lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags is not the trailing-90-day figure POL-RD-06 asks for and I do not use it.

The money is arithmetic and it is bounded. Charged total was SGD 33.36; the POL-RD-02 recomputation against the booked optimal route gives SGD 24.2240; the difference is SGD 9.136, rounded up to SGD 9.15. That is 27.4% of the charged total, far below the 90% share that alone converts a partial into a FULL_REFUND, so the ruling value should be PARTIAL_REFUND and not FULL_REFUND. Because SGD 9.136 exceeds the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor, NO_ACTION is not available either.

The rider's separate head of complaint - the 'extra ERP charge' - must not be paid twice. The POL-RD-02 recomputation includes only the on-optimal-route gantry (Pioneer Road inbound, SGD 1.00) and excludes the off-route gantry (Tuas South Avenue 8 loop, SGD 2.00), so that SGD 2.00 is already returned inside the SGD 9.136 refund. POL-RD-09(1) says off-route ERP is comprehended in the POL-RD-02 figure and must never be added on top of it; it may be itemised in the ruling for transparency, but the total payable to the rider cannot exceed SGD 9.15.

I do not ask the judge to run POL-RD-03 or POL-RD-04, because the record does not carry them. POL-RD-03 needs a traffic_advisory, and EV-ADVIS-09111-01 is MISSING with weight 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT - no advisory matched the booked route and trip window. POL-RD-04 needs a rider instruction, and the chat log carries only the rider asking the driver to rejoin the booked route, with waypoint_hint null on the message. The driver's own statement that he 'followed the road available to me' is a general assertion which POL-RD-08 says does not discharge the driver's burden. The dispute therefore comes down to quantum, and the quantum on this record is SGD 9.15.

ruling.explanation:
Rider and driver — the trip did deviate, and part of what the rider paid is returned: SGD 9.15.

Deviation (POL-RD-01). The governing measurement is the vehicle's own GPS trace, not the rounded copy on the trip record: trace_distance_km 16.2 km against the booked optimal_distance_km 12.0 km. That is an excess of 4.2 km, or 35%, clearing both establishment tests (greater than 20% and greater than 0.8 km). It does not reach the MATERIAL bands — 35% is below 50% and 4.2 km is below 8.0 km — so the POL-RD-06 driver-profile check is not engaged; in any event it would clear the driver, deviation_flags_90d being 0 across completed_trips_90d of 610.

No excuse applies. POL-RD-03 cannot run: the only traffic advisory, EV-ADVIS-09111-01, is MISSING, weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, so no closure or contraflow is on file for the booked route and window. POL-RD-04 cannot run: the chat log (EV-CHAT-09111) contains the rider asking the driver to rejoin the booked route, not any request to detour, and the message carries no waypoint_hint, so the corroboration test is undecidable and the clause is unavailable. Neither endpoint was amended (POL-RD-05) and the vehicle was RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL (POL-RD-12). The driver's 'I followed the road available to me' cites no artifact and does not discharge his shifted burden under POL-RD-08.

Money (POL-RD-02), on the METERED fare. Charged total: SGD 33.36. Recomputed fare on the booked optimal route: SGD 24.2240 = ((3.80 base + 0.75 x 12.0 km + 0.28 x 24.0 min) x 1.2 surge) + 0.80 platform fee + 1.00 on-optimal-route ERP - 1.00 promo discount. Refund: 33.36 - 24.2240 = SGD 9.1360, rounded UP to SGD 9.15. That is 27.4% of charged_total, far below the 90% share that alone converts a partial into a full refund, and above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor. The result is PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 9.15 — the amount the rider contested.

The 'extra ERP' is itemised but not paid twice. The SGD 2.00 'Tuas South Avenue 8 loop' line is off the optimal route and is already excluded from the recomputed fare, so it is returned inside the SGD 9.15; POL-RD-09(1) forbids adding it on top. The SGD 1.00 'Pioneer Road inbound' gantry lies on the optimal route and stays in the recomputed fare. Total ERP charged was SGD 3.00.

Confidence is 0.9, against a POL-GEN-02(2) cap of 1.0 because the deciding facts rest on the GPS trace, the trip record and the fare breakdown, each at weight 1.0. The profile artifacts were used only as POL-GEN-01 allows; rating, account age and the lifetime counters play no part in the outcome.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and the driver: the trip did run long, and the arithmetic is fixed by the record.

Deviation. The platform's own GPS trace (EV-GPS-09111) measures 16.2 km against the 12.0 km booked optimal route on the trip record (EV-TRIP-09111) — an excess of 4.2 km, or 35%. Both POL-RD-01 establishment tests pass (over 20% and over 0.8 km), so the deviation is ESTABLISHED on the trace itself. The trace is clean for policy purposes (205 fixes at 10-second spacing, 100% coverage, no gaps, max gap 0), so POL-RD-07 imposes nothing and no independent corroboration is needed. The excess does not reach the MATERIAL band (more than 50% or more than 8.0 km); at 35% and 4.2 km it stays below both. The POL-RD-06 driver-profile check therefore does not engage, and no driver-conduct referral arises; in any event driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 across 610 trips, so there is no repeat pattern. The lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags mentioned in the driver's papers is context only under POL-GEN-01 and is not used as a ground.

Exoneration. Nothing excuses the excess. The only traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-09111-01) is MISSING, weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT, so POL-RD-03 cannot run. The chat log (EV-CHAT-09111) contains no rider detour instruction — the rider's only message asks the driver to return to the booked route and its waypoint_hint is null — so POL-RD-04 is unavailable. No endpoint was amended (POL-RD-05) and the trip was not pooled (POL-RD-12). The driver's statement that he 'followed the road available' is a general assertion citing no artifact and invoking no clause; under POL-RD-08 it does not discharge the driver's shifted burden.

Money. Charged total was SGD 33.36. The recomputed optimal-route fare is SGD 24.2240: base fare 3.80 + 0.75 x 12.0 km + 0.28 x 24.0 min = 19.520, surged at 1.2 = 23.424, + 0.80 platform fee + 1.00 on-route ERP (Pioneer Road inbound) - 1.00 promo discount. Refund = 33.36 - 24.2240 = SGD 9.1360, rounded UP to SGD 9.15. That is 27.4% of the charged total — below the 90% share that alone would make it a FULL_REFUND — and well above the SGD 0.50 de minimis. Part of the contested amount is therefore returned.

The 'extra ERP charge' the rider raised is already inside that refund. The SGD 2.00 'Tuas South Avenue 8 loop' line is off-optimal-route and is excluded from the recomputed fare, so it is comprehended in the SGD 9.136; under POL-RD-09(1) it is itemised for transparency only and is never added on top of the POL-RD-02 figure.

Billing integrity. Neither charged gantry is crossed by the trace under POL-RD-09(4)'s 250 m rule: 'Pioneer Road inbound' (SGD 1.00) has its nearest fix 912 m away, 'Tuas South Avenue 8 loop' (SGD 2.00) 1646 m away. That is recorded as a billing-integrity finding and referred for review. Because these are the only unmatched charge lines, POL-RD-10(8) does not escalate, and no POL-RD-10 trigger otherwise fires (identifiers match, the trace is unimpaired, and the refund is far below the ceiling).

Rider's profile. rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0, so no enhanced corroboration is demanded.

Confidence 0.90. The findings rest on the GPS trace, trip record and fare breakdown, each at full weight 1.0; the missing advisory carries no fact and caps nothing.

Outcome: PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 9.15 to the rider.
referrals: POL-RD-09(4) billing-integrity review: the two ERP charge lines on EV-FARE-09111 are not matched by the GPS trace under the 250 m crossing rule — 'Pioneer Road inbound' (SGD 1.00) has its nearest fix 912 m away and 'Tuas South Avenue 8 loop' (SGD 2.00) 1646 m away. Verify the pass-through ERP lines (the off-route SGD 2.00 is already comprehended in the POL-RD-02 refund and is not added to it).

It is not, however, MATERIAL: 35% is under the 50% band and 4.2 km is under the 8.0 km band. Nothing excuses it — the only traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-09111-01) is MISSING at weight 0.0 so POL-RD-03 cannot run; the chat log (EV-CHAT-09111) carries no rider detour request and waypoint_hint is null, so POL-RD-04 does not run; neither endpoint was amended (POL-RD-05); and the trip was not pooled (POL-RD-12). On the METERED fare POL-RD-02 gives: charged_total SGD 33.36; recomputed_fare SGD 24.2240 (3.80 + 0.75×12.0 + 0.28×24.0 = 19.52, surged ×1.2 = 23.424, + 0.80 platform fee, + 1.00 on-optimal-route ERP, − 1.00 promo); refund SGD 9.1360, rounded UP to SGD 9.15 — above the SGD 0.50 de minimis and far below the 90% full-refund share. ruling.explanation:
To the rider and the driver. This is a genuine route deviation, and the money is arithmetic.

Deviation. The GPS trace is complete and unimpaired for policy purposes — 205 fixes at 10-second intervals, 100% coverage, no gap over 30 seconds, max gap 0 — so POL-RD-07 imposes nothing and the deviation can be established on the trace alone. The trace measures 16.2 km against a booked optimal route of 12.0 km, an excess of 4.2 km (35%). Both POL-RD-01 tests pass (above 20% and above 0.8 km), so the deviation is ESTABLISHED. It is NOT material: 35% is below 50% and 4.2 km is below 8.0 km, so the POL-RD-06 driver-profile check is not engaged — and it would clear the driver anyway, because driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 across completed_trips_90d of 610, below both the 3-flag and 0.05-ratio thresholds. No exculpatory clause applies: the traffic-advisory artifact EV-ADVIS-09111-01 is MISSING (weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT), so POL-RD-03 cannot run; the chat log (both messages, waypoint_hint null) records no rider instruction to detour, so POL-RD-04 is unavailable; no endpoint was amended (POL-RD-05); and vehicle_type is RYDE_X, not pooled (POL-RD-12). The driver's statement that he 'followed the road available to me' cites no artifact and no clause and, under POL-RD-08, carries no weight.

Refund. Charged total: SGD 33.36. Recomputed fare against the booked optimal route: SGD 24.2240 (= (3.80 + 0.75 x 12.0 km + 0.28 x 24.0 min) x 1.2 surge = 23.424, + 0.80 platform fee + 1.00 on-optimal-route ERP - 1.00 promo discount). Refund = 33.36 - 24.2240 = SGD 9.1360, rounded up to SGD 9.15. That is 27.4% of charged_total, below the 90% share that alone would make it a FULL_REFUND, and above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor. The result is a PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 9.15 — the amount contested.

ERP. The SGD 3.00 charged is the SGD 1.00 'Pioneer Road inbound' gantry (on the optimal route) plus the SGD 2.00 'Tuas South Avenue 8 loop' gantry (not on the optimal route). The SGD 2.00 is already comprehended inside the POL-RD-02 refund and is never added on top (POL-RD-09(1)). Applying the POL-RD-09(4) match test — a gantry is crossed only where a fix lies within 250 m — the trace never comes within 1,645.74 m of the Tuas South Avenue 8 loop gantry, so that line is a billing-integrity finding and is recorded in the referrals; it adds no money, because the same SGD 2.00 is already returned inside the refund. The Pioneer Road inbound line is the optimal-route ERP the recomputation itself consumes (matching trip_record.optimal_route_erp_sgd of SGD 1.00), so after the refund the rider's net ERP cost is the fair SGD 1.00 and no further standalone correction arises.

Profiles were used only as POL-GEN-01 permits: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d / completed_trips_90d for POL-RD-06, and rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d / deviation_claims_60d_substantiated for POL-RD-08 (both 0, so no corroboration beyond the trace is required). One rider claim — that the driver's statement fails to discharge his shifted burden, citing EV-ADVIS-09111-01 without its issue code — was discarded by the referee for undisclosed impairment and is not relied on; the same conclusion is reached independently by POL-RD-08's rule that an uncited assertion carries no weight.
referrals: POL-RD-09(4): billing-integrity finding — the SGD 2.00 'Tuas South Avenue 8 loop' ERP line is a charge for a gantry the GPS trace never passes (nearest fix 1,645.74 m, beyond the 250 m match radius). The amount is already comprehended in the POL-RD-02 refund and is not added again; the finding is recorded for billing review.

ledger.claim: The trip deviated on the platform's own measurement. The GPS trace records trace_distance_km of 16.2 km against a booked optimal_distance_km of 12.0 km — an excess of 4.2 km, or 35% — which clears both POL-RD-01 tests: greater than 20% of the optimal distance and greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms. The deviation is therefore ESTABLISHED on this trip's own evidence, and the driver's assertion that he 'followed the road available' does not meet either test in reverse.

The trace is clean for policy purposes, so no impairment consequences attach. It carries 205 fixes at a 10-second interval with 100% coverage, an empty gaps list and max_gap_sec of 0. None of POL-RD-07 limbs (a) to (c) fires, the deviation may be established on the gps_trace alone, and no independent corroboration is needed to carry it.

The rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08 is discharged. The trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry trip_id TRP-09111 and describe the same journey, and the excess measured above meets the POL-RD-01 threshold from an unimpaired trace. The burden therefore shifts to the driver to point to a specific artifact and clause.

No rider instruction exonerates the driver under POL-RD-04. The chat log holds exactly two messages: the rider at 08:12:00 writing 'The navigation route was left after Pioneer Road. Please return to the booked route', and the driver at 08:12:35 replying 'I am following the road ahead'. There is no waypoint_hint and no road or place requested by the rider, so POL-RD-04 is unavailable and the whole excess stands.

No traffic advisory excuses the deviation under POL-RD-03. The only advisory artifact, EV-ADVIS-09111-01, is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT — it carries no payload, so no road closure or contraflow is on file for the booked route and window, and POL-RD-03(a) to (c) cannot be satisfied. The artifact is cited for its absence, which is itself a citable fact.

Neither endpoint was amended, so POL-RD-05 gives the driver no relief and the baseline remains the booked 12.0 km. pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are null and amended_optimal_distance_km is null, so no re-quote exists and no distance falls to be excluded on this ground.

This was not a pooled trip, so POL-RD-12's matched-itinerary baseline does not apply. vehicle_type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, and solo_optimal_distance_km is null; the booked optimal of 12.0 km is the correct baseline for the threshold test and for the recomputation.

The refund is arithmetic, not discretionary. The fare model is METERED and quoted_fare_sgd is null, so POL-RD-02 governs and POL-RD-11 does not: charged_total is SGD 33.36; recomputed_fare is SGD 24.2240 (base 3.80 + 0.75 x 12.0 km + 0.28 x 24.0 min = 19.520, surged at 1.2 to 23.424, + 0.80 platform fee + 1.00 on-optimal-route ERP - 1.00 promo discount); the refund is 33.36 - 24.2240 = SGD 9.1360, rounded UP to SGD 9.15. That is 27.4% of charged_total, below the 90% full-refund share, so the outcome is a PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 9.15 — precisely the amount the rider contests.

The off-route gantry charge is already captured and must not be added twice. The SGD 2.00 'Tuas South Avenue 8 loop' line is flagged on_optimal_route false and sits outside the recomputed fare, which includes only the SGD 1.00 'Pioneer Road inbound' gantry lying on the optimal route. Under POL-RD-09(1) that off-route ERP is comprehended in the POL-RD-02 refund and is itemised for transparency only — it is never added on top of the POL-RD-02 figure.

The record confirms the stakes for the rider, who filed this dispute. payment_status is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.0, so the rider is presently carrying the full SGD 33.36. NO_ACTION would leave that charge standing and the rider out of pocket for a deviation the platform's own trace measures at 35%; only a refund leaves the rider not carrying the disputed excess.

No enhanced corroboration is demanded of this rider. rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0, far below the four-claim trigger in POL-RD-08, and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0; the rider is not a serial unsubstantiated claimant, and no additional source beyond the trace is required to carry this claim.

The driver's statement does not discharge the shifted burden. 'I followed the road available to me. The rider did not request any stop' names no traffic_advisory, cites no artifact and invokes no clause; under POL-RD-08 a general assertion unsupported by an advisory ID carries no weight, and the rider's own on-trip message records that the driver was told he had left the booked route and continued anyway.

But the same figures keep this trip out of the MATERIAL band, because 35% is below the 50% figure and 4.2 km is below the 8.0 km figure. The rider's description of the trip as 'substantially longer' therefore overstates it: the deviation is established but not material, the POL-RD-06 driver-profile check is not engaged, and the POL-RD-06(b) uplift to FULL_REFUND is unavailable.

Even if the profile check were run, the only two counters POL-RD-06 permits clear the driver: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 across driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 610 - no flags against the 3-flag threshold, and a zero ratio against the 0.05 threshold. There is no repeat-deviation pattern, so POL-RD-06(a) tie-breaking, POL-RD-06(b) uplift and POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral all fail at the first step. I rely on those two fields alone, as POL-GEN-01 requires; the lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags is not the trailing-90-day figure POL-RD-06 asks for and I do not use it.

ledger.claim: The money is arithmetic and it is bounded. Charged total was SGD 33.36; the POL-RD-02 recomputation against the booked optimal route gives SGD 24.2240; the difference is SGD 9.136, rounded up to SGD 9.15. That is 27.4% of the charged total, far below the 90% share that alone converts a partial into a FULL_REFUND, so the ruling value should be PARTIAL_REFUND and not FULL_REFUND. Because SGD 9.136 exceeds the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor, NO_ACTION is not available either.

The rider's separate head of complaint - the 'extra ERP charge' - must not be paid twice. The POL-RD-02 recomputation includes only the on-optimal-route gantry (Pioneer Road inbound, SGD 1.00) and excludes the off-route gantry (Tuas South Avenue 8 loop, SGD 2.00), so that SGD 2.00 is already returned inside the SGD 9.136 refund. POL-RD-09(1) says off-route ERP is comprehended in the POL-RD-02 figure and must never be added on top of it; it may be itemised in the ruling for transparency, but the total payable to the rider cannot exceed SGD 9.15.

I do not ask the judge to run POL-RD-03 or POL-RD-04, because the record does not carry them. POL-RD-03 needs a traffic_advisory, and EV-ADVIS-09111-01 is MISSING with weight 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT - no advisory matched the booked route and trip window. POL-RD-04 needs a rider instruction, and the chat log carries only the rider asking the driver to rejoin the booked route, with waypoint_hint null on the message. The driver's own statement that he 'followed the road available to me' is a general assertion which POL-RD-08 says does not discharge the driver's burden. The dispute therefore comes down to quantum, and the quantum on this record is SGD 9.15.
